chunks: Aban, from Abdul Rahman ibn Abu Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the child steals and has not yet reached puberty (bed-wetting), the ends of his fingers are cut.
He said, and Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'It was done by none except the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and myself.'

key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: Child (specifically one who has not reached puberty)
key_terms.يَحْتَلِمْ: To reach puberty / to wet the bed (sign of maturity)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for theft committed by a child who has not reached puberty in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the hadd penalty for pre-pubescent children who commit theft, distinguishing it from adult theft by amputating only the ends of the fingers rather than the hand. It highlights the unique authority of the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali to implement this specific judicial measure, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the application of fixed penalties to minors who possess sufficient discernment (mumayyiz).

en.hubeali:
Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘When the child steals and he has yet to bed-wet, the ends of his fingers would be cut’.
And Ali<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It has not been done except by Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> and myself<sup>asws</sup>’.
